Eight 20-foot-tall sculptures depict fantastic creatures from the spirit world, imagined through Mexican magical realism. Designed and created by Mexican artists and artisans, these brightly colored animals represent the powerful animal guardian spirits of Mesoamerican folklore. Inspired by Mexico City artist Pedro Linares, each sculpture is an enlarged reproduction of original works by celebrated Oaxacan artists. The exhibition pays tribute to the exceptional craftsmanship of Mexican artisans, celebrates Mexico’s rich cultural heritage, and highlights the connections between Houston and the nation across the Gulf.

event_description: Nominated for seven Tony Awards, including “Best Musical,” this inspiring true story proves that everyday acts of kindness are heroic in themselves. On the morning of September 11, 2001, 7,000 travelers suddenly find their flights rerouted to Gander, Newfoundland, doubling the tiny town’s population overnight. A moment of fear and uncertainty soon becomes an extraordinary story of generosity, hospitality, and human connection. As the townsfolk open their hearts and homes to the stranded passengers from all over the world, once-strangers become friends that shine light even through the darkest moments. The lively, uplifting musical that took Broadway by storm comes to town for its Houston-produced debut in signature Stages style.

event_name: Beyond the Hedges: Historias de Latinidad at Rice University
event_description: Rice University is home to a campus bounded by historic hedges but deeply interconnected with the dynamic metropolis of Houston, one of the most diverse and culturally expansive global cities in the world. While the university was originally chartered exclusively for Houston’s white inhabitants, trailblazing Latines defied those boundaries from the beginning. They walked through the Sallyport, refusing to be kept out. Pieced together from photos, letters, and diaries discovered in the archives of the Woodson Research Center and the Houston Public Library Special Collections, and from oral histories of the students, staff, and faculty who shaped both Rice and the city, this exhibit proves that from the moment ground broke in 1910, Latine individuals have helped shape Rice’s legacy. Today, nearly 13.5% of Rice University’s undergraduate students and more than 44% of Houston’s residents are of Latin American descent. Beyond the Hedges: Historias de Latinidad at Rice University honors this community, which has, for over a century, dedicated their brilliance, service, resilience, and creativity to the campus and the city.

event_description: About the Performance Season Opening Concert: Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony Celebrate the Texas Medical Center Orchestra’s first concert of the 2026–2027 season with one of the most inspiring and beloved works in the orchestral repertoire. Beethoven’s Symphony No. 9. A landmark of classical music, Beethoven’s final symphony is renowned for its monumental scale, emotional depth, and triumphant “Ode to Joy” finale, offering a timeless celebration of hope, unity, and the enduring human spirit. The evening begins with Overture to Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg by Richard Wagner. A vibrant and uplifting work that sets the stage for an unforgettable musical journey. From its stirring opening to its exhilarating choral finale, this concert celebrates the power of music to unite performers and audiences alike. To conclude this mesmerizing evening, the orchestra will perform Symphony No. 9 in D minor by Ludwig van Beethoven. Featured in this symphony are Sophia Orrico, Soprano; Antoinette Pompe van Meerdervoort, Mezzo-Soprano; Stefán Víkingur, Tenor; and Tzvi Bat Asherah, Bass-Baritone and The Kingwood Chorale, under the direction of Todd Miller. Founded in 2000 by Maestra Libi Lebel, the Texas Medical Center Orchestra (TMCO) is one of the few community orchestras in the United States rooted in the medical community. Comprised of physicians, nurses, researchers, healthcare professionals, educators, students, and accomplished musicians from across Greater Houston, TMCO is dedicated to presenting exceptional orchestral performances while supporting medically related and educational charities. Nationally recognized for its artistic excellence through honors from The American Prize, the orchestra continues to enrich Houston’s cultural landscape while advancing its mission of service through music. Through the shared language of music, TMCO inspires, connects, and strengthens the communities it serves. Program: Richard Wagner: Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg Overture Ludwig van Beethoven: Symphony No. 9 in D minor Featured Artists: Sophia Orrico, Soprano Antoinette Pompe van Meerdervoort, Mezzo-Soprano Stefán Víkingur, Tenor Tzvi Bat Asherah, Bass-Baritone Kingwood Chorale *Please note, that any contributions made during the purchase path will go directly to Performing Arts Houston.* Box Office provided by Performing Arts Houston, in partnership with Houston First Corporation

He has been named one of Variety’s “Top 10 Comics to Watch,” one of Vulture’s “Comedians You Should and Will Know,” and in their “Best Comedy of 2025” roundup, The New York Times honored him with Best Range. He was recently awarded Comedy Performance of the Year for his latest special at the 2026 Just for Laughs Festival. His debut stand-up special Hell, produced by Jax and Jen Statsky, is streaming on Peacock. On the horizon, Chris will appear in the upcoming feature The Comeback King starring Glen Powell, produced and directed by Judd Apatow. He will also be in upcoming feature The Catch, alongside Emma Stone and Chris Pine.

About the Performance Born in Tuscany, Matteo Bocelli, son of the legendary Andrea Bocelli, was immersed in music from an early age. He made his live performance debut at just eighteen years old at Rome’s iconic Colosseum, signaling the arrival of a remarkable new talent. Matteo first captured international attention in 2018 with “Fall On Me,” his acclaimed duet with his father featured in Disney’s The Nutcracker and the Four Realms . The song has since amassed more than 400 million streams worldwide. Building on that success, he released his self-titled debut album, Matteo , in 2023 and has gone on to perform on some of the world’s most prestigious stages, including the 96th Academy Awards, the Sydney Opera House, and Madison Square Garden. In early 2026, he was crowned King of the Viña del Mar International Song Festival, further cementing his growing global profile. Released in September 2025 on Decca Records, Matteo’s second album, Falling in Love , represents a significant artistic evolution. Recorded at his home in Tuscany with renowned producer Martin Terefe, the album seamlessly blends his classical roots with a warm, contemporary sound. Matteo co-wrote every original song alongside an acclaimed group of collaborators, including Grammy Award winner Amy Wadge, Toby Gad, Iain Archer, and Johan Carlsson. Many of the songwriting sessions unfolded around shared meals at his Tuscan home, lending the album a deeply personal and intimate character. The record concludes with Matteo’s heartfelt interpretation of “Caruso,” Lucio Dalla’s timeless masterpiece, which has become a defining moment of his live performances. Over the past several years, Matteo has steadily established himself as an artist in his own right, earning international acclaim through performances around the world and collaborations with artists such as Ed Sheeran. While honoring his family’s extraordinary musical legacy, he has remained committed to developing a voice, style, and repertoire that are uniquely his own. As Matteo reflects, “Being a Bocelli is both a privilege and a responsibility. I’ve never wanted to run from my father’s incredible legacy, but I do want people to hear my voice, my emotions, and my version of love.” His live show moves effortlessly between soaring ballads and uplifting contemporary songs, performed in both English and Italian.
